text:
Dear Dr. Henderson,

Thank you for agreeing to see this young male patient in consultation. His difficulties first became apparent during his first year of life, when he began experiencing multiple repeated bouts of infection, mainly involving the upper respiratory tract. 

Recent routine evaluations revealed a diffuse depression across all three peripheral cell lines. His laboratory profile demonstrates a significant reduction in his red cell count and hemoglobin, an absolute neutrophil count that is persistently and markedly depressed, and platelet numbers that are profoundly reduced. In light of these peripheral findings, an aspirate and core biopsy were recently obtained; the evaluation revealed marked hypoplasia with diminished overall cellular content for his age, alongside clear dysplastic changes noted among the developing hematopoietic lines. 

On physical examination today, he is afebrile with normal vital signs. He is active and comfortable. His heart sounds are regular without murmurs, his chest is clear bilaterally, and his abdomen is soft and non-tender with no palpable liver or spleen enlargement. There is no peripheral lymphadenopathy or skin rash. He lives at home with both parents, attends daycare part-time, and has reached normal developmental milestones. His family history is unremarkable, with no known early-onset blood conditions. He is currently not taking any chronic medications other than an age-appropriate daily multivitamin.

Given his early-onset presentation, trilinage cytopenias, and the hypoplastic changes with dysplasia seen on his marrow studies, I would greatly value your comprehensive assessment and guidance on how best to proceed with his evaluation and care.

Warm regards,

Dr. Robert Miller
